title: Open `<details>` and `<dialog>` if their content is targeted in the URL fragment

labels.name: needs implementer interest
labels.description: Moving the issue forward requires implementers to express interest

body:
This is related to https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/3567 and came up here, https://mastodon.social/@Edent/109346907540120433. Consider the following markup: ```html
Super-Important

I am currently invisible

``` and a URL pointing to that document with the fragment `#jump-here`. On page load the content will not be visible and even not be part of the DOM at all. The same situation appears with the `` element. Parts of the document are not linkable to anymore, although being present in the plain text markup. For one, this weakens the concept of an URL being able to point to content with sub-document granularity. And for another it makes for bad UX, if a visitor follows a link and won’t see the content linked to. Even worse, they might end up on a completely different part of the document (i.e. the top, when the `
` element is possibly somewhere lower below the fold). Possible ways to mitigate the problem: 1. If the content of a `
` or `` element is referenced, assume an implicit `open` attribute. Advantage: very easy, very comprehensible behavior. Disadvantage: No opt-out possibility for developers. 2. Allow opening via CSS. If we assume a new property `open-state`, the rule ```css details:has(:target) { open-state: open; } ``` allows to opt-in to an auto-opening behavior. Advantage: good control for developers. Disadvantage: If the stylesheet does not load, the content is still hidden. 3. Force opening via new fragment identifier syntax. E.g., `#:~:open=jump-here`. I list this only for completeness, since it merges the worst of both worlds above, no opt-out for developers while at the same time making it harder to link to a fragment.
